messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager | KV_CACHE_EVICTION_RATE high on serving-pool-us-west-2 (threshold breach). root_tx=svc-gen-3 -> paging alex (oncall).

maria (prod-eng): seeing a spike in 5xx and latency for hosted gen endpoints, looks correlated with recent func/tool structured output spike. paging alex — can you confirm?

alex (oncall): on it, joining now. grabbing metrics. can you drop the query that reproduces?

maria (prod-eng): minimal repro: many requests with structured toolcall payloads (variable 'tools' array shape). KV cache miss ratio -> 92% on the batchers. sample log: 
```
2028-10-02T13:00:12Z svc-gen-3 WARN cache: miss key=kvc:v2:hash(....) reason=shape_change
2028-10-02T13:00:12Z svc-gen-3 INFO batcher: flush id=7 size=1 latency=345ms
2028-10-02T13:00:13Z svc-gen-3 ERROR model: request_timeout
```

alex (oncall): ouch. that flush size=1 indicates continuous batching fragmentation. what changed recently? any config rollouts?

nick (platform): We flipped a small rollout earlier today: `enable_structured_toolcall_v2=true` on hosted pool - target 10% traffic. Could be related.

samira (ml-infra): structured tool outputs are higher-variance in token length and include top-level tool metadata; that can break prefix caching heuristics and change KV keys if we include schema fingerprints in cache key. hypothesis: schema variability => cache churn => tiny batches and higher latency.

alex (oncall): ok immediate mitigations: 1) remove canary flag 2) lower continuous_batch_max_tokens and max_wait_ms 3) route traffic to fallback model. I'll start 1 now.

alex (oncall): rolling back canary: `platformctl rollout-set serving-pool-us-west-2 enable_structured_toolcall_v2=false --force --reason "pager rollback"`

incident-bot: Rollback job submitted (job_id=rb-1834567201-1). Notifying deploy agents.

kevin (sre): taking over oncall in 5. can you paste KV eviction metric graph link?

maria (prod-eng): https://metrics.redwood/graph?kvc_evictions&range=30m — eviction spike aligns with rollout at 12:58 UTC. Affected tenants: 4 high-throughput customers, some 5xx and timeouts, others degraded latency.

alex (oncall): rollback finished; monitoring. initial evictions dropping but some backpressure remains. lowering batching config on pool now:
```
api update-pool-config --pool serving-pool-us-west-2 --set continuous_batch_max_tokens=256 --set continuous_batch_max_items=16
```

samira (ml-infra): also recommend disabling schema-fingerprint from cache key until we can normalize tool output shape. quick patch: flip `cache_use_schema_fp=false` on the batcher. This avoids key churn but weakens collision protection — acceptable as emergency.

nick (platform): issuing patch to batcher config now. `cfgctl set serving.batchers.cache_use_schema_fp false --env hosted --pool us-west-2`

helpdesk-bot: Notifying support channels and creating incident ticket INC-2028-3342 with summary "KV cache cascade due to structured tool outputs".

maria (prod-eng): customer impact: 4 tenants > 5x latency, 2 tenants hit request timeouts; window ~12:58–13:12 UTC. SLA risk flagged. please prepare post-incident comms.

kevin (sre): observed tail latencies improving after rollback + batch config. miss ratio down from 92% -> 18% in 8 minutes. still watching.

samira (ml-infra): running eval to confirm structured outputs won't reintroduce churn when re-enabled: need to canonicalize toolcall outputs (stable ordering + fixed metadata keys). will open MR with sanitizer.

alex (oncall): handing off to kevin — I have to step out for the deploy window in 10m. state: rollback done, batch config lowered, schema_fp disabled, evictions trending down.

kevin (sre): taking charge. I’ll keep monitoring for 30m. setting incident severity to Sev2 and adding timeline to the ticket. assigning action items: samira -> sanitizer MR, nick -> gated rollout plan, maria -> customer comms draft.

maria (prod-eng): drafting notice for affected customers: short summary, what we changed, ETA for full re-enablement once sanitizer lands.

samira (ml-infra): MR created: `ml-infra/normalize-tool-output` — adds stable sort to tools array + strips non-deterministic fields before caching. request review from nick and kevin.

nick (platform): reviewing now. also will add a canary gating check that measures cache_key_entropy before enabling structured toolcall.

kevin (sre): current numbers: eviction_rate 18%, average batch size 4.2 -> baseline was ~12. latency is trending toward normal. keeping pager open until stable 15m window.

helpdesk-bot: Support notification sent to #support-affected-customers and ticket updated with mitigation steps.

maria (prod-eng): quick note for postmortem: root cause = schema/shape variability in new structured toolcall v2 creating cache key churn and continuous batch fragmentation. Contributing factors: rollout without cache-key stability check, no entropy gate in canary.

kevin (sre): agreed. action items (short): 1) revert canary gating logic (nick) 2) MR sanitizer + tests (samira) 3) add metric-based canary gate (nick) 4) run against synthetic workload before re-enable (maria) 5) update runbook for toolcall rollouts (kevin).

alex (oncall): thumbs up. I’m clear to mark incident as "mitigated" if numbers remain stable for next 15m. :white_check_mark:

kevin (sre): will update timeline and close pager when stable. creating postmortem draft now and assigning owners.

maria (prod-eng): thanks all — ping me if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2028-3342 status: Mitigation in progress. Pager still active.

kevin (sre): final note before I close: estimated customer impact window 14 minutes, approximate affected qps 8% of hosted API. severity assessment: degraded SLAs but no data loss. full postmortem to follow.

maria (prod-eng): adding link to draft postmortem: https://docs.redwood/incidents/INC-2028-3342/draft

kevin (sre): closing handoff — monitoring continues.
